subject: Streaming TTFT & latency MAP for Orchard Health - perf plan + results
messages:
From: Kate Smith <kate.smith@orchard.health>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@orchard.health>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: MAP: perf targets we need included (TTFT + streaming latency)

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the product looked promising. As we scope the MAP, the procurement and security teams need a clear performance evaluation included in the mutual action plan. Specifically we want:

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) measured both server-side (server receive -> first token emit) and observed client-side (HTTP start -> first byte).
- Streaming latency distributions (p50/p95/p99) for the first token and per-token steady state.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) at different concurrency levels (1, 5, 10, 25).
- A concurrency sweep showing tail latency impact and recommended production config (batching, kv-cache warm policies).

Can you confirm Redwood can run these tests against the model we discussed (redwood-chat-3b-quant) and share a proposed test plan + target dates? Our target is to finish the evaluation and sign by Jan 31 so we can start integration in early Feb.

Tom and I would like a small summary table in the MAP showing p50/p95/p99 TTFT at the key concurrency points. Also please include raw artifacts (CSV) so our SRE can validate.

Appreciate it —
Kate

Kate Smith
Director of Product
Orchard Health
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Smith <kate.smith@orchard.health>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@orchard.health>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: MAP: perf targets we need included (TTFT + streaming latency)

Hi Kate — thanks, and great question. We can absolutely include a performance benchmarking appendix in the MAP and produce both summary tables and raw CSVs. Below is the proposed evaluation plan and schedule; I attached a draft MAP (Orchard_MAP_v1.pdf) and the perf_test_matrix.csv with the exact combinations we plan to run.

Proposed evaluation plan (high level):
- Test model: redwood-chat-3b-quant (the same quantized checkpoint from the demo).
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated sandbox in us-east-1 (GPU A100 80GB equiv), isolated VPC.
- Workloads: 3 prompt families representative of your use cases (clinical note summarization, triage chat, quick Q&A).
- Generation config: streaming=true, max_tokens=512, temperature=0.2, top_p=0.9.
- Sequence lengths: prompt 128 tokens; target 256 and 512 generation lengths for throughput sensitivity.
- Concurrency sweep: single-client concurrency targets [1, 5, 10, 25].
- Metrics collected: server-side TTFT, client-observed TTFT, per-token latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, 95% mem/gpu utilization, error rates.
- Artifacts: results_summary_YYYYMMDD.pdf + raw_results CSVs + plots.

Schedule:
- Jan 12: test harness + seed runs (low concurrency)
- Jan 13: full concurrency sweep (1,5,10,25) across three prompt families
- Jan 14: analysis and summary deliverable (PDF + CSVs)
- Jan 17: MAP update with perf appendix and recommended production config

Next steps: please confirm the prompt families (I attached examples in the CSV) and confirm permission to run tests in the dedicated sandbox on the proposed dates. Once you confirm, Marcus and Marissa will run the harness and I’ll own the MAP update and timeline coordination.

Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kate Smith <kate.smith@orchard.health>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@orchard.health>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 15:30:00 -05:00
Subject: Perf runs complete — initial summary + attachments

Hi all,

We completed the test matrix this morning against redwood-chat-3b-quant in the dedicated sandbox. Attaching results_summary_20270112.pdf (key charts + callouts) and raw_results_20270112.zip (CSV per run). Below is the compact summary table you asked for (server-side TTFT measured from request_receive -> first_token_emit; client-observed TTFT measured from TCP connect+TLS->first_byte). All numbers in milliseconds.

Test conditions: streaming enabled, prompt=128 tokens, gen=256 tokens, batching disabled to reflect low-latency config, KV cache warmed by pre-seeding 10 requests. Cores: single-model pod; GPU ~75% utilization at concurrency 10.

Summary — TTFT (server-side / client-observed):
- Concurrency 1: p50 28 / 35 ms, p95 62 / 78 ms, p99 118 / 153 ms
- Concurrency 5: p50 31 / 39 ms, p95 86 / 112 ms, p99 172 / 219 ms
- Concurrency 10: p50 36 / 44 ms, p95 120 / 156 ms, p99 260 / 338 ms
- Concurrency 25: p50 62 / 74 ms, p95 260 / 315 ms, p99 540 / 670 ms

Steady-state per-token latency (after first token) — median per-token emit: 8 ms; p95 18 ms; p99 34 ms (single model pod, streaming path). Tokens/sec observed (aggregate per pod): ~1,400 tok/s at concurrency 10, ~2,100 tok/s at concurrency 25 (due to batching effects at higher client QPS).

Notes and recommendations:
- For sub-100ms TTFT at p95 in production at concurrency 10, we recommend:
  - Enable small-scale continuous batching with max_batch_size=8 and latency_budget=12ms to reduce p95 on token throughput-heavy flows.
  - Keep KV-cache warm via a short-lived warm pool (we used 10 warm instances in these runs).
  - If you expect sustained concurrency >10, provision additional dedicated pods (N+1) to preserve tail latency.

Caveats: these runs were in a controlled sandbox; network variability in your VPC and end-user access patterns will change client-observed numbers. We included raw latency traces in the ZIP so your SREs can re-check distributions.

Attaching: results_summary_20270112.pdf, raw_results_20270112.zip

— Marcus Lin
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

On Tue, 12 Jan 2027 at 15:30 Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> We completed the test matrix this morning against redwood-chat-3b-quant in the dedicated sandbox.

Thanks Marcus — this is very helpful and in line with expectations. Two quick follow-ups:

1) For our production integration, what’s the recommended canary ramp schedule (requests/min or concurrency targets) you’d suggest to validate latency SLOs without risking user-facing errors?
2) Are there any config toggles you’d advise disabling for clinical data paths (e.g., any extra telemetry that could add overhead)?

If you can include a short canary plan in the MAP appendix we’ll review with SRE and procurement.

— Tom
Senior SRE, Orchard Health
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Smith <kate.smith@orchard.health>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@orchard.health>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jan 2027 11:20:00 -05:00
Subject: MAP update and next steps — timeline to close

Hi Kate & Tom —

Thanks for the quick review. I’ve updated the MAP appendix with Marcus’s results and our recommended canary plan; attaching the MAP (Orchard_MAP_v1.pdf) and pointing to the results artifacts. Highlights:

- Canary ramp: start at concurrency=1 for 1 hour (smoke), ramp to 5 over 30 mins, hold 2 hours, ramp to 10 over 60 mins, validate p95 TTFT and error rate thresholds. If p95 > 200ms or error_rate > 0.5% at any hold, rollback and open an incident.
- Prod config recommendations: continuous small batching (max_batch_size=8), KV cache warm pool of 5 per-pod, per-route rate limits to avoid thundering bursts.
- Timeline to close: finalize MAP + SOW by Jan 20, DocuSign execution Jan 22–24, integration test window Jan 25–29, go/no-go Jan 31, production rollout Feb 1–3.

We also noted a minor procurement ask — a short one-page SLA addendum for latency targets at commissioning. I’ll loop Legal once you confirm.

Please confirm if the timeline matches your procurement calendar and I’ll schedule a 30-minute MAP walkthrough for Mon Jan 17.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193
